about.title: San Carlos Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Falls happen fast, but the aftermath rarely feels that way. Whether you slipped on a wet floor near El Camino Real, tripped on uneven pavement close to Holly Street, or fell on poorly maintained steps at a rental property, the days after can bring pain, missed work, and confusion about what comes next. California law asks injured people to show that a property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and didn't fix it or warn visitors. That's why documenting the scene, photographing the hazard, and pushing for preserved surveillance footage matters so much, especially in a city where many falls happen inside retail spaces or shared residential buildings with cameras that record over footage within days. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves. We simply connect San Carlos residents with an independent attorney from our network who can evaluate the claim and explain what evidence-gathering looks like for your specific situation, at no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Fall Victims in San Carlos Turn to LawProactive

items.title: We Understand the Notice Requirement
items.desc: California premises cases hinge on whether the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. The attorney we connect you with can help identify maintenance records, prior complaints, or inspection logs that speak to that notice.

items.title: We Push for Fast Evidence Preservation
items.desc: Surveillance footage at San Carlos businesses and apartment complexes is often overwritten within days, so timing matters. Connecting quickly with an attorney can mean the difference between video evidence existing or being gone.

items.title: We Account for Comparative Fault
items.desc: California allows recovery even if you were partly at fault for a fall, though your share of responsibility can reduce compensation. An independent attorney can help make sure your side of the story is documented accurately from the start.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in San Carlos?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a premises liability lawsuit. If a government entity, like the City of San Carlos, owns or maintains the property, the deadline is much shorter and involves a separate claims process. It's worth having an attorney review the property ownership as soon as possible.

items.question: What if I was partly to blame for my fall?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning you can still recover damages even if you share some responsibility, though your compensation may be reduced by your percentage of fault. This is common in fall cases where footwear, lighting, or distraction come into question. An independent attorney can help present the facts fairly.

items.question: I fell at a business near El Camino Real. What should I do first?
items.answer: Try to photograph the hazard before it's cleaned up or repaired, and ask the business to preserve any surveillance video, since many systems automatically erase footage within days or weeks. Get the names of any witnesses and seek medical attention even if injuries seem minor at first. Reporting the incident and getting documentation started early can matter a great deal later.
